title: Can Several Minimal Findings Reveal a Hidden Attribute? An Exactly Solvable Pilot on Linked, Coarsened and Task-Output Releases, with a Release-Audit Toolkit (code, fixtures, results and paper)
description:
A reproducible pilot and a reusable, standard-library Python toolkit (python3 -m release_audit) for measuring how much small sets of structured findings passed between workflow stages reveal about an attribute that none of them states.

The pilot uses a fictional two-stage household workflow with a hidden three-level reserve band. On 3,000 test households it compares one release, two linked releases, a declared coarsening of the linked releases and the report-checklist answers alone, against trained attackers and exactly computed Bayes-optimal ceilings, with a task-tied utility measure. The toolkit takes a JSON description of a pipeline and reports exact leakage, a per-field information budget, Pareto-optimal release designs and, for labelled records, cross-validated estimates.

Run python3 run_pilot.py to reproduce every result. Code: MIT. Paper, protocol, fixtures, examples and results: CC BY 4.0. All data are synthetic.
